channel.title: The Nevada Independent - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from The Nevada Independent (thenevadaindependent.com)

item.title: Comunidad, dividida acerca de cambios en horario de inicio de clases en escuelas del Condado Clark
item.description: Mientras que algunos padres de familia y personal elogian al distrito por el cambio, otros se preocupan por las interrupciones en las actividades extraescolares de los estudiantes y la carga que podría suponer para los padres que trabajan.

item.title: Nevada will pay $19M more for SNAP this year. It’s taking steps to avoid further costs.
item.description: New federal rules are requiring states to pay more of SNAP's administrative costs, provide food assistance to fewer residents and curb erroneous payments.

item.title: One Vegas casino's plan to win back Canadians: a favorable currency exchange rate
item.description: Will Trump’s latest tirade against our northern neighbor put a crimp in efforts to boost downtown visitation? Also, Bally’s offers a Vegas project timeline.

item.title: Lombardo’s office declines lawmaker’s request to attend meeting on Musk’s Boring Co.
item.description: In a rare move, the governor’s office has declined an invitation from the chair of the state’s Interim Committee on Growth and Infrastructure to provide more details about the regulation of Elon Musk’s controversial Boring Company project in Southern Nevada.

item.title: Funcionarios de educación superior de Nevada lamentan aumento en colegiatura
item.description: Líderes del sistema de educación superior de Nevada dijeron que los incrementos en la colegiatura eran necesarios para cubrir un déficit presupuestario anual de casi $50 millones de dólares.

item.title: ‘This one is different’: Cortez Masto says GOP must separate DHS bill to avoid shutdown
item.description: The senator, who criticized Kristi Noem, said she would consider the facts and “make an appropriate decision at that time” if the DHS secretary is impeached.

item.title: OPINION: MAGA goes from ‘Don’t tread on me’ to ‘Govern me harder’
item.description: Unleashing thousands of hastily trained federal agents onto American streets with guns, masks and “immunity” should have always been considered a step too far for any serious constitutional conservative.

item.title: It’s a mild winter in Nevada. Here’s how that could end up hitting your pocketbook.
item.description: While Nevada is renowned for its lack of precipitation, there’s a hidden cost behind the seemingly endless streak of mild days and clear blue skies.

item.title: ‘A challenging environment’: Vegas Strip gaming and tourism struggled in 2025
item.description: Visitation slides to 2021 levels, casinos barely hit the ledgers’ positive side and the airport suffers steep passenger declines. Meanwhile, locals markets shine.

item.title: 45,000 Nevadans expected to lose food stamp benefits in March, says state agency
item.description: Reduced eligibility for SNAP assistance is just one way the food program is changing. Starting in October, states will also have to pay more to administer benefits and may be penalized for high payment error rates.
